summary: As of November 13, 2026, junk-bond spreads are 3.23 percentage points and are down 0.19 percentage points over five trading days. Investment-grade spreads are down 0.04 percentage points over those same five trading days. The CCC-minus-BB gap is 11.30 percentage points. Of the 0.14 percentage-point move in the all-in junk yield, 0.19 was the credit spread and 0.33 was Treasury rates. The 10-year yield is 5.15 percent as of November 13, 2026 and the 30-year is 5.47 percent as of November 13, 2026, a gap of 0.32 percentage points. Brent is 91.65 dollars a barrel as of November 17, 2026 (+0.17 percent over five trading days), and the curve is an unpublished curve shape. The 5-year inflation breakeven is 2.25 percent as of November 16, 2026, down 0.04 percentage points over five observations. The 10-year real yield is 2.91 percent as of November 13, 2026. The broad dollar index is 122.65 as of November 13, 2026, +1.08 index points over 20 observations. VIX is 19.30 as of November 13, 2026. The Fed balance sheet is 6.76 trillion dollars as of November 11, 2026, up 3 billion dollars over the latest four weekly observations. Reserve balances are 2.96 trillion dollars as of November 11, 2026, down 62 billion dollars over the latest four weekly observations. Overnight reverse repo is 0.182 billion dollars as of November 16, 2026, down 0.07 billion over the latest four observations.
